rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A soul stabilized in spiritual ascent is protected from reverting to natural and human traits and from descending to the commanding self.
rows.anchor: فمن كان متمكنا في مقام الترقي تخلص من التنزل إلى مقام النفس الأمارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The serene soul is illuminated by the heart, leaves blameworthy traits, and adopts noble character.
rows.anchor: النفس المطمئنة هي التي تنورت بنور القلب حتى تخلت عن صفاتها الذميمة

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: The soul is at peace through remembering God, grateful for blessing, and patient in hardship.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي) : أي نفس آرام كرفته بذكر من كه شاكر بودي در نعمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God addresses the believer honorably, either directly as He spoke to Moses or through an angel, after the reckoning is complete.
rows.anchor: بالذات للمؤمن إكراما له كما كلم موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام أو على لسان الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning to the Lord means reaching the promised honor and nearness; this figurative destination defeats corporealists' argument and indicates the spirit was created first.
rows.anchor: أي إلى ما وعد لك من الكرامة والزلفى فكونه تعالى منتهى الغاية إنما هو بهذا الاعتبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul is pleased with its enduring bliss and accepted by God.
rows.anchor: بما أوتيت من النعيم المقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joining God's elect is spiritual happiness, while entering paradise with them is bodily happiness; another reading takes the soul as spirit reentering the bodies it left at resurrection.
rows.anchor: فالدخول في زمرة الخواص هي السعادة الروحانية والدخول معهم في الجنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some place the address at death; a report says the Prophet told Abu Bakr that an angel would say it to him when he died.
rows.anchor: أبا بكر رضي الله عنه سأل عن ذلك رسول الله فقال : إن الملك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: When God intends to take the soul, it is at peace with God and pleased with Him, and God is pleased with it.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن إذا أراد الله قبضها اطمأنت إلى الله ورضيت عن الله ورضى الله عنها

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر رضي الله عنهما
rows.claim: At a believer's death, angels welcome the fragrant soul, present it to God, place it among believers, and its grave is widened and lit; the disbeliever receives a foul gift and is summoned to Hell.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمر رضي الله عنهما إذا توفى العبد المؤمن أرسل الله ملكين

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير رحمه الله
rows.claim: At Ibn Abbas's funeral in Taif, an extraordinary bird entered his bier and was never seen leaving; the verse was recited at his grave.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير رحمه الله مات ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما بالطائف فشهدت جنازته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse that God takes souls at death shows that some blessed souls are taken directly by God.
rows.anchor: ودل قوله تعالى الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها إن من النفوس الظبية من يتولى الله قبضها

rows.speaker: بعض أهل الإشارة
rows.claim: The soul settled in worldly life is told to return to God by abandoning it and following the path of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض أهل الإشارة يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة إلى الدنيا ارجعي إلى الله بتركها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is counted as twenty Meccan verses, though some classify it as Medinan except for its first four verses.
rows.anchor: عشرون آية مكية أو مدنية إلا أربع آيات من أولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening لا is redundant in the oath, as confirmed by the oath over the secure town in the Sura of the Fig; in Persian the sense is simply that God swears.
rows.anchor: لا صلة دل عليه إن الله اقسم بالبلد الأمين في سورة التين

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Alternatively, لا strengthens the oath, like the Arab expressions No, by God, I did not do it and No, by God, I will do it.
rows.anchor: وفي "كشف الأسرار" لا لتأكيد القسم كقول العرب لا والله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A town is a bounded place shaped by its inhabitants gathering and settling there; its plurals are بلاد and بلدان.
rows.anchor: والبلد المكان والمحدود المتأثر باجتماع قطانه وإقامتهم فيه وجمعه بلاد وبلدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mecca deserves the oath because it is a safe sanctuary, the Prophet's birthplace, Abraham's sanctuary, Ishmael's home, the universal qibla, and pilgrimage expiates a lifetime of sins.
rows.anchor: ثم إن الله تعالى اقسم بمكة لفضلها فإنه جعلها حرما آمنا ومسقط رأس النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about the Prophet is circumstantial, and hill means residing in Mecca; his presence adds honor to an already noble city and exposes the Meccans' folly in trying to expel him.
rows.anchor: أي والحال إنك لا يا محمد حال في مكة نازل بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A place gains honor from its noble occupant, and the Prophet called Medina طابة because it became good through him; sacred places associated with him deserve respect.
rows.anchor: فما لا شرف فيه يحصل له شرف بشرف المكين وما فيه شرف ذاتي يحصل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Persian verses praise the Kaaba, Medina, and the plain of Mecca as made more radiant and honorable by the Prophet's arrival.
rows.anchor: أي كعبه را زيمن قدوم توصد شرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In inward interpretation, Mecca signifies embodied human existence and the Messenger signifies the heart hidden in the body's left side.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى بلد مكة الوجود الإنساني وإلى رسول القلب المستكن في الجانب الأيسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father is Abraham, and the indefinite wording magnifies him; what he fathered is Ishmael.
rows.anchor: والمراد به إبراهيم عليه السلام والتنكير للتفخيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to Quraysh leaders who especially troubled the Prophet, such as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
rows.anchor: كالوليد بن المغيرة وإضرابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weakened إن and its noun fill the two complements of حساب; the fool assumes no one can exact revenge, but God can and is a mighty avenger.
rows.anchor: إن مخففة من الثقيلة سادة مع اسمها مسد مفعولي الحسبان أي يحسب إن الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boastful speaker says he spent great heaps of wealth for reputation; pre-Islamic Arabs called such ostentation generosity and honor, though the word squandered shows it is truly wasted.
rows.anchor: أنفقت كقول العرب خسرت عليه كذا إذا أنفق عليه

rows.speaker: عائشة رضي الله عنها
rows.claim: Aisha asked whether Abdullah ibn Judan's pre-Islamic charity and care for kin would benefit him; the Prophet answered that it would not, since he never sought forgiveness for Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: ما قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها في حق عبد الله ابن جدعان كان في الجاهلية

rows.speaker: رسول الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet said the charitable deeds would not benefit Abdullah ibn Judan because he never prayed for forgiveness on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: لا ينفعه لأنه لم يقل يوما رب اغفر لي خطيئتي يوم الدين

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A person will not move on Judgment Day until questioned about his lifespan, wealth's source and spending, deeds, and love for the Prophet's family.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث لا تزول قدما العبد يوم القيامة حتى يسأل عن أربع عن عمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God saw the man's spending and knew his corrupt intention, and will judge it; ostentatious spending is a vice mistaken by the ignorant for virtue.
rows.anchor: يعني إن الله رآه واطلع على خبث نيته وفساد سريرته وإنه مجازيه عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eyes let a person see the visible world from earth to heaven, distinguish benefit from harm, and view the world, Qur'an, and signs of God.
rows.anchor: يبصر بهما عالم الملك من الأرض إلى السماء حتى يشاهد بهما في طرفة عين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eye is a bright mirror that receives images; its small pupil, rapid movement, lids, and lashes protect sight and keep out flies and vermin.
rows.anchor: نحرس ابدن من الآفات وهي نيرة كالمرءآة إذ قابلها شيء ارتسمت صورته فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eyes sit in the head like a lamp on a beacon and come as a pair like sun and moon; dark brows and pupils reduce glare, while black lashes strengthen sight.
rows.anchor: وجعلها ثنتين كالشمس والقمر فإنهما عينا التعين الدنيوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account links black clothing to looking at white marble, whose brightness weakens sight, and says antimony strengthens vision.
rows.anchor: ولذا قال عليه السلام في الأثمد إنه يقوي البصر وجعل الحدقة محركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The movable pupil sees in different directions without turning the neck, and the two eyes share one level so a single object is not seen twice.
rows.anchor: وجعل النظارين جميعا على خط مستقيم عرضا ولم يقع واحد منهما أعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pair of eyes also signals an outer and an inner eye, both of which should be guarded because binocular sight is more complete.
rows.anchor: وفي العينين إشارة إلى العين الظاهرة والعين الباطنة فينبغي أن يحافظ على كلتيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tongue conveys thoughts, enables transactions and testimony, and tastes; without it, gesture or writing would make life difficult.
rows.anchor: يترجم به عن ضمائره وبه تنعقد المعاملات وتحصل الشهادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because hearing and sight are needed more often than speech, the single tongue teaches restraint and speaking only for good; lips help a person stop needless words.
rows.anchor: وإنما تعدد العين والأذن وتفرد اللسان لأن حاجة الإنسان إلى السمع والبصر أكثر

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Umar used to keep a stone in his mouth so that he would avoid speaking about matters that did not concern him.
rows.anchor: وقد حكه عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه إنه كان يجعل في فمه حجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inner tongue is the heart's capacity for inward conversation; corrupting inner perception also ruins this readiness, as the Persian admonition warns against polluted sight.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى لسان القلب فإنه يتكلم به بالمفاوضة القلبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lips cover the mouth for silence and assist speech, eating, drinking, and blowing; the upper lip also keeps floating dirt out of a drink.
rows.anchor: يستر بهما فاه إذا أراد السكوت ويستعين بهما على النطق والأكل

rows.speaker: السجاوندي
rows.claim: The lip is singled out because most letters emerge from it.
rows.anchor: قال السجاوندي خص الشفة لروج أكثر الحروف منها

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A prophetic report says God gave a person two lips and two eyelids as means to close the mouth and eyes when tempted by forbidden speech or sight.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث إن الله يقول ابن آدم إن نازعك لسان فيما حرمت عليك فقد أعنتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report calls the private parts, ears, hands, and feet trusts, and says faith is absent from whoever lacks trustworthiness.
rows.anchor: وفي الخبر الفرج أمانة والأذن أمانة واليد أمانة والرجل أمانة والإيمان لمن لا أمانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those on the right receive their records in their right hands, are led rightward to Paradise, and are people of goodness and happiness whose obedience benefits themselves and others.
rows.anchor: أي اليمين وهم الذين يعطون كتهم بإيمانهم ويسلك بهم من طريق اليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative points to the righteous as present before God in honor, showing their rank and exalted station.
rows.anchor: وفي اسم الإشارة دلة على حضورهم عند الله في مقام كرامته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's signs mean the proofs He established for truth, whether scripture, argument, or the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: بما نصبناه دليلا على الحق من كتاب وحجة أو بالقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic pronoun marks the unbelievers' fall from the honor of God's presence and their deserved concealment.
rows.anchor: في ضمير الغالب دلالة على سقوطهم عن شرف الحضور وإنهم أحقاء بالإخفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The left-handed receive records in their left hands or behind their backs and are led leftward to Hell; they are people of evil and misery whose disobedience harms themselves and others.
rows.anchor: أي الشمال وهم الذين يعطون كتبهم بشمائلهم ومن وراء ظهورهم وسلك بهم شمالا إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire's doors are shut forever: no one exits, and neither relief nor breath enters; the omitted noun is doors, reflected in the word's inflection.
rows.anchor: خبر مقدم لقوله نار مؤصدة أي نار أبوابها مغلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With hamza, مؤصدة is the passive of آصدت; without it, the word derives from أوصدت, though it may also reflect a hamza shifted to waw after a damma.
rows.anchor: فمن قرأها مؤصدة بالهمزة جعلها اسم مفعول من آصدت ومن لم يهمزها

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن عباس
rows.claim: The transmitter of Asim disliked the hamza in this word and wished to cover his ears when hearing it, apparently preserving it from his teacher without hamza.
rows.anchor: وكان أبو بكر بن عباس راوي عاصم يكره الهمزة في هذا الحرف

rows.speaker: القراء
rows.claim: The reciters report that Hafs preserved the hamza and that this reading is more precise for the letter than Abu Bakr's, despite Abu Bakr's stature in hadith.
rows.anchor: وقد حفظه حفص بالهمزة وهو أضبط لحرف من أبي بكر على ما نقله القراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In inward interpretation, the fire of veiling, abandonment, and loss is sealed shut over the commanding soul.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى إن نار الحجاب والخذلان والخسران مؤصدة على نفس الأمارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth was spread out on every side over water so its inhabitants could live there; الطحو means spreading like الدحو, with ط substituted for د.
rows.anchor: ومن بسطها من كل جانب على الماء كي يعيش أهلها فيها والطحو كالدحو بمعنى البسط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning created things in oaths does not equate them with God in reverence; their ordered sequence lets reason infer the maker's existence and power.
rows.anchor: وأفراد بعض المخلوقات بالذكر وعطف الخالق عليه والأقسام بهما ليس لاستوائهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun's light, relation to the moon, appearance at daybreak, and covering by night, followed by heaven's encompassing path, move thought from sensible greatness to the Creator's majesty.
rows.anchor: أقسم بالشمس التي هي أعظم المحسوسات شرفا ونفعا ووصفها بأوصافها الأربعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and heaven change and move, so they are contingent bodies that depend on a powerful, wise maker; inwardly they signify the heaven of spirits and earth of bodies.
rows.anchor: فتوسل العقل بمعرفة أحوالهما وأوصافهما إلى كبرياء صانعهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul is something God originated and created with readiness for its perfections; the indefinite form magnifies it or denotes the many souls, and may refer to Adam's soul.
rows.anchor: أي ومن أنشأها وأبدعها مستعدة لكملاتها والتنكير للتفخيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge of the unseen Creator is inferred from the visible world: heaven, earth, and especially ensouled beings, the noblest composite creatures.
rows.anchor: والشاهد ليس إلا العالم الجسماني وهو إما علوي بسيط كالسماء وأما سفلى بسيط كالأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attached clauses show that no hidden word for Lord should be supplied before the oaths; the implied wording would falsely make the objects themselves the subjects of the oath.
rows.anchor: إذا المقدر في المعطوف عليه يقدر في المعطوف فيكون التقدير ورب ما بناها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ف in فألهمها may express causation after the soul's formation or sequence after its outward and inward faculties were completed.
rows.anchor: الفاء إن كانت لسببية التسوية فالأمر ظاهر وإن كانت لتقبها فلعل المراد منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inspiration is a thought placed in the heart from God or the highest realm; its root conveys swallowing something.
rows.anchor: والإلهام القاء الشيء في الروع إما من جهة الله أو من جهة الملاء الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fujur breaches religion's veil; it precedes taqwa for the verse's rhyme or because suppressing sin is especially urgent, and the soul can choose either path.
rows.anchor: والفجور شق ستر الديانة قدم على التقوى لمراعاة الفواصل أو لشدة الاهتمام

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Some elders say inspiration is only for good: the soul is shown sin to avoid and piety to practice, since God never commands evil.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الكبار الإلهام لا يكون إلا في الخير فلا يقال في الشر الهمني الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form انبعث responds to بعث, as in saying that someone was urged toward a matter and responded.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لا يخفى إن محل الإلهام هو النفس

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another explanation says permissible acts are not inspired because they belong to the soul by nature from the moment it is created.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم لم ينسب سبحانه إلى النفس خاطر المباح ولا إلهامه فيها

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: All souls share one underlying reality and differ with changing states: orientation to God is serene, to nature commanding, and alternation between them self-reproaching.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : تدل الآية على كون النفوس كلها حقيقة واحدة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس رضي الله عنهما
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet said purifying the self purifies the heart: when desire is cleansed from the self, the heart is freed from attachment to everything besides God.
rows.anchor: وابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ، روايت كرده كه حضرت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God creates and decrees human acts, an act is attributed to its human agent, as one says Zayd struck rather than God struck.
rows.anchor: وكون أفعال العبد بتقدير الله تعالى وخلقه لا ينافي إسناد الفعل إلى العبد

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Purifying the soul earns praiseworthy traits and reward; purification is attributed to the servant's effort, God as true agent, the means such as charity, or worship as its instrument.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : وبزكاء النفس وطهارتها يصير الإنسان بحيث يستحق في الدنيا

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Khaba means to fail, lose, be deprived, or miss one's aim; dassa derives from repeated concealment, with the final doubled consonant assimilated to ي.
rows.anchor: في "القاموس" خاب يخب خيبة حرم وخسر

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib defines d-s-s as forcing one thing into another; hiding the soul means burying it in sins.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب : الدس إدخال الشيء في الشيء بضرب من الإكراه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The loser diminishes and conceals the soul through sin and unleashes it into natural appetites.
rows.anchor: والمعنى قد خسر من نقصها وأخفاها بالفجور وبإرسالها في المشتهيات الطبيعية

rows.speaker: شيخي وسندي
rows.claim: The author's spiritual master interprets the soul here as the essential, all-inclusive reality.
rows.anchor: وقال شيخي وسندي قدس سره في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tribe of Thamud is the subject; their denial confirms that burying the soul through tyranny is among the gravest forms of self-corruption.
rows.anchor: المراد القبيلة ولذا قال وهو استئناف وارد لتقرير مضمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun طغوى is used in place of the more common طغيان to match the verse endings; Kashf al-Asrar explains its altered form by noun and adjective patterns.
rows.anchor: والطغوى بالفتح مصدر بمعنى الطغيان إلا أنه لما كان أشبه برؤوس الآيات اختير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ب may mark cause, so Thamud denied because of their rebellion; the verb may be intransitive or omit the known object, their prophet Salih.
rows.anchor: والباء للسببية أي فعلت التكذيب بسبب طغيانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another grammatical reading makes ب connect to the denial: they denied the threatened punishment, the overpowering cry described elsewhere as a طاغية.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الباء صلة للتكذيب أي كذبت بما أوعدت به من العذاب ذي الطغوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means when the most wretched Thamudi rose, Qudar ibn Salif, responding to the one who sent or urged him; انبعث means he obeyed the call.
rows.anchor: أي حين قام أشقى ثمود وهو قدار بن سالف امتثالا لأمر من بعثه إليه

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Kashf al-Asrar defines انبعاث as hurrying into obedience to whoever urges the person.
rows.anchor: فإن انبعث مطاوع لبعث يقال بعثت فلانا على أمر فانبعث له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ashqa can refer to one or several; the verse about their calling their companion and his killing the camel shows one man acted while all shared blame through approval.
rows.anchor: فإن أفعل التفضيل إذا أضيف يصلح للواحد والمتعدد والمذكر والمؤنث ويدل على الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger is Salih ibn Ubayd ibn Jabir ibn Thamud ibn Aws ibn Iram; calling him Messenger signals the duty to obey and the depth of their defiance.
rows.anchor: وهو صالح عليه السلام ابن عبيد بن جابر بن ثمود بن عوص بن أرم فالإضافة للعهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naqat Allah is an accusative warning formula; the camel belongs to God honorifically and proves His unity, power, and Salih's prophethood, so they must not harm it.
rows.anchor: منصوب على التحذير وإن لم يكن من الصور التي يجب فيها حذف العامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The camel had an assigned share of water on one day while Thamud and their livestock drank on another, which they resented.
rows.anchor: فإنها كان لها شرب يوم معلوم ولهم ولمواشيهم شرب يوم آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They denied Salih's warning against harming the camel, then the most wretched man killed it; the whole tribe shares the act because they approved, and العقر means cutting its throat.
rows.anchor: أي الأشقى والجمع على تقدير وحدته لرضى الكل بفعله

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli names Qudar ibn Salif as the killer, Qadira as his mother, and Musda ibn Wihrawa ibn Jahm as his accomplice.
rows.anchor: قال السهيلي العاقر قدار بن سالف وأمه قديرة وصاحبه الذي شاركه في عقر الناقة

rows.speaker: رسول الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet told Ali that the most wretched of the earlier people was the camel's killer and the most wretched of later people would be Ali's killer.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث قال عليه السلام لعلي يا علي أتدري من أشقى الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In inward interpretation the she-camel is the soul, slain by carnal darkness and animal desire; Ali embodied the Prophet's spirituality, so killing him targeted Muhammad, the universal mercy.
rows.anchor: وذلك الناقة إشارة إلى ناقة الروح فكما أن عقرها بالظلمة النفسانية والشهوات الحيوانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Damdam means to enclose and cover completely; repeating د intensifies the encompassing, as shown by the sequence دممت ثم دمدمت in Kashf al-Asrar.
rows.anchor: فأطبق عليم العذاب وهو الصيحة الهائلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase because of their sin explicitly warns every sinner; leveling them means none escaped, young or old, or that Thamud were flattened to the ground.
rows.anchor: والتصريح بذلك مع دلالة الفاء عليه للإنذار بعاقبة الذنب ليعتبر به كل مذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the people saw signs of punishment, they sought to kill Salih, but God saved him and the believers through His mercy.
rows.anchor: طلبوا صالحا عليه السلام أن يقتلوه فأنجاه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening و is either resumptive or circumstantial, referring to God as He leveled them without fearing the aftermath of punishment or their destruction.
rows.anchor: الواو للاستئناف أو للحال من المنوى في فسواها الراجع إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike human rulers who fear consequences and show some mercy, God acts justly and need not fear the result of a just act.
rows.anchor: كما يخاف سائر المعاقبين من الملوك والولاة فيترحم بعض الترحم وذلك أن الله تعالى لا يفعل إلا بحق

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another reading says the killer did not fear what followed the camel's slaughter, despite Salih having warned them of the calamity and punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ولا يخاف هواي قدار ولا هم ما يعقب عقرها

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: God did not stop the inward flow of prophethood and messengership or the inward flow of sainthood to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : ما ودعك ربك بقطع فيض النبوة والرسالة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The afterlife is enduring and unclouded while the first life is transient and mixed with harm; the terms also signify the honors of each life.
rows.anchor: لما إنها باقية صافية عن الشوائب على الإطلاق والأولى أي الدنيا لأنها خلقت قبل الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lam is emphatic lam of initiation, not an oath; the suppressed subject is You, and lam plus سوف assures a gift certain to arrive after a wise delay.
rows.anchor: اللام للابتداء دخلت الخبر لتأكيد مضمون الجملة والمبتدأ محذوف تقديره ولأنت

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Prophet's final spiritual states are better and more complete than his initial acts, as the completion of religion indicates.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : يعني أحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise includes worldly gifts such as perfected character, knowledge, public success, conquests, and Islam's spread under the Prophet and later Muslim rulers, as well as unknown honors stored for him.
rows.anchor: والآية عدة كريمة شاملة لما أعطاه الله في الدنيا من كمال النفس وعلوم الأولين

rows.speaker: رسول الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet described a thousand white-pearl palaces in Paradise, with musk for soil.
rows.anchor: وقد أنبأ عنسمة منها قوله عليه اسلام لي في الجنة ألف قصر من لؤلؤ أبيض

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Prophet was found unique like an orphaned pearl, endowed with singular readiness, detached from all else, and gathered in the station of divine oneness.
rows.anchor: يا ديد ترا كوهرى يكانه كه بكمال قابليت ازهمه كائنات منفرد بودي

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: A unique pearl is the image: the Prophet had no equal in Quraysh's nobility, and God sheltered and protected him among his enemies.
rows.anchor: وفي "الكشاف" ومن بديع التفاسير أنه من قولهم درة يتيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ضال means lacking revealed laws and rulings that reason cannot discover and can only learn through transmission; it can also mean absent.
rows.anchor: معنى الضلال فقدان الشرائع والخلو عن الأحكام التي لا يهتدي إليها العقول

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib says ضلال can mean any deviation, intentional or accidental and slight or great, so it applies to prophets and unbelievers in radically different senses.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : يقال الضلال لكل عدود عن المنهج عمدا كان أو سهوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guided Muhammad to revealed law through scripture and taught him what he had not known; this favor began after orphanhood, when he already used sound judgment, worshipped no idol, and committed no indecency.
rows.anchor: أي فهداك إلى مناهج الشرائع في تضاعيف ما أوحى إليك من الكتاب المبين

rows.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
rows.claim: One interpretation makes the people the ones who were astray: God found the Prophet among them and guided them through him.
rows.anchor: وفي الأسئلة المقحمة معناه ووجدك بين ضالين فهداهم بك

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: A Sufi interpretation takes the Prophet's lostness as bewilderment in divine transcendence, then guidance as complete knowledge after sobriety following annihilation and ecstasy.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : أي متحيرا في تيه الألوهية

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس رضي الله عنهما
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that as a boy Muhammad was lost in Mecca's ravines; Abd al-Muttalib sought him in prayer, and Abu Jahl returned him, so God saved him through an enemy as with Moses and Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ، إن النبي عليه السلام ضل في شعاب مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عائلا means poor, supported by Ibn Masud's reading عديما; God aided Muhammad through Khadija's wealth or spoils until he could give away a hundred camels.
rows.anchor: أي فقيرا يؤيده ما في مصحف عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report that provision was placed under the Prophet's spear shows that his supremacy over wealthy rulers came from God, not inherited riches; another view says God enriched his heart with contentment.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث جعل رزقي تحت ظل رمحي وفيه إشارة إلى أن عليه السلام ، لو

rows.speaker: رسول الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet said true wealth is richness of the self, not having abundant property.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام ليس الغنى عن كثرة العرض ولكن الغنى غنى النفس

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib glosses enrichment as removing inward poverty and granting the greater wealth of a rich soul.
rows.anchor: ولذا قال الراغب : أي أزال عنك فقر النفس وجعل لك الغنى الأكبر

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Inwardly, the Prophet was poor through annihilation of ego and became rich through abiding in God's presence, essence, names, and attributes.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : أي فقيرا فانيا عن أنيتك وأنانيتك

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Qushayri distinguishes metaphorical wealth through growing possessions for common people from true wealth through purified spiritual states for the elect.
rows.anchor: قال الامام القشيري رحمه الله أغناء الله عباده على قسمين فمنهم نم يغنيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True poverty is abandoning everything besides God and surrendering one's existence; this is the poverty in which the Prophet took pride.
rows.anchor: فالفقر الحقيقي هو التخلي عما سوى الله وبذل الوجود وما يتبعه وهو الذي وقع الافتخار به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The listed favors are meant to steady the Prophet's heart after revelation's interruption, not merely to boast of blessings.
rows.anchor: ليس الامتنان بل تقوية قلبه عليه السلام للاطمئنان بعد التوديع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object اليتيم is fronted before its verb after the conditional أما; the ف is causal, and قهر means either overpowering or humiliating.
rows.anchor: والقهر الغلبة والتذليل معا ويستعمل في كل واحد منهما

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The heart that seeks immersion in divine reality should not be rebuked for needing this rest from prophetic burdens, as in the Prophet's tender address to Humayra.
rows.anchor: أي لا تنهر سائل قلبك عن الاستغراق في بعض الأوقات في بحر الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speaking of God's gifts is verbal gratitude and reminds others; the gifts include those already granted and promised, especially prophecy, guidance, and teaching law and wisdom.
rows.anchor: فإن تحديث العبد وأخباره بنعمة الله شكر باللسان وتذكير للغير

rows.speaker: صاحب فتوحات
rows.claim: The beloved is intrinsically beloved and the benefactor is usually thanked; hearing of God's gifts draws people toward loving Him, making them His beloved as He loves them.
rows.anchor: صاحب فتوحات قدس سره آورده كه نعمت يزيست محبوب بالذات ومنعم در أغلب شكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final command corresponds to the preceding favor and rounds out three parallel directives; declaring blessings follows the cleansing of not oppressing or rebuking.
rows.anchor: وهذا الثالث بمقابلة الثاني وهو قوله ووجدك ضالا فهدى آخر لمراعاة الفواصل

rows.speaker: الكواشي
rows.claim: Al-Kawashi says recounting God's blessings is meritorious when one is safe from showing off and ego and hopes others will follow; others dislike it from fear of temptation.
rows.anchor: قال في "الكواشي" رأى بعض التحدث بنعم الله

rows.speaker: عين المعاني
rows.claim: A report says recounting blessings is gratitude and leaving it is ingratitude; another advises concealing blessings from the envious.
rows.anchor: وفي "عين المعاني" قال عليه السلام : التحدث بالنعم شكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Legal guidance favors concealing charity for a sick person wary of heirs or for someone fearing oppressive rulers will learn his wealth.
rows.anchor: وفي الأشباه أي رجل ينبغي له أخفاه إخراج الزكاة عن بعض دون بعض

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says to recount a blessing inwardly so one remembers God's past and present favor; if outward blessings may be mentioned, inward gifts and divine communications may too.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية في الآية حدث به نفسك أي لا تنسى فضله عليك قديما وحديثا

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib says شرح originally means cutting or spreading flesh, then opening the chest with divine light, tranquility, or spirit; it also means unfolding obscure speech to expose hidden meanings.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : الشرح بسط اللحم ونحوه يقال شرحت اللحم

rows.speaker: رسول الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A prophetic report says when light enters the heart it expands, can bear trials, and preserves the secret of lordship.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث إذا دخل النور في القلب انشرح أي عاين القلب وانفسح

rows.speaker: موسى عليه السلام
rows.claim: Moses prayed for an expanded heart so he could endure opponents' foolishness and stubbornness without distress.
rows.anchor: موسى عليه السلام ، رب اشرح لي صدري أي وسع قلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added لك signals the benefit is for the Prophet; the negative question affirms that his heart was opened to unseen and seen realities and could receive and convey them.
rows.anchor: وزيادة لك للإيذان بأن الشرح من منافعه ومصالحه عليه السلام وإنكار النفي إثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Physical ties did not block spiritual illumination, nor public concerns absorption in God; the Prophet united presence with people and presence with God.
rows.anchor: فما صدك الملابسة بالعلائق الجسمانية عن اقتباس أنوار الملكات الروحانية

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Inwardly, the heart opens through prophethood's light and the burdens of calling both worlds, the secret expands through messengership, and the light of sainthood realizes divine knowledge and truth.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : يشير إلى انفساح صدر قلبه بنور النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's outward chest was opened several times: at age five or six to remove a dark satanic mark, at the start of revelation, and on the night journey.
rows.anchor: وأما شرح الصدر الصوري فقد وقع مرارا مرة وهو ابن خمس أو ست

rows.speaker: رسول الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: In the night-journey report, Gabriel opened the Prophet's chest to his navel, Michael brought Zamzam to wash it, then a golden vessel of wisdom and faith filled and restored his heart.
rows.anchor: در حديث آمده كه شب معراج جبريل مرا تكيه داد واز بالاي سينه تانافمن بشكافت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masters prescribe beginning a seeker's practice with the remembrance لا إله إلا الله, striking across the chest to break the devil's share and desires until light fills the space; constant remembrance opens the heart.
rows.anchor: قال المشايخ لا بد للطالب في ابتداء أمره أن يشتغل بذكر لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Removing the burden means lifting its heavy load; placing عنك before the object hastens the good news and makes the reader anticipate it.
rows.anchor: أي حططنا وأسقطنا عنك حملك الثقيل وعنك متعلق بوضعنا وتقديمه على المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The burden made the back creak; dictionaries explain أنقض as breaking noisily or weighing someone until the load's saddle parts groan under its weight.
rows.anchor: أي حمله على النقيض وهو صوت الانتقاض والانفكاك كما يسمع من الرحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The burden may be the Prophet's distressing lapses before prophethood, lack of detailed rulings, or grief and pity over opponents who rejected his call; God lifted it through pardon and teaching.
rows.anchor: مثل به حاله عليه السلام ، مما كان يثقل عليه ويغمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes lifting the burden a metaphor for the Prophet's protection from sin and purification from stain.
rows.anchor: وقد يجعل قوله ووضعنا عنك وزرك كناية عن عصمته من الذنوب وتطهيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raised the Prophet's mention by granting him the title and rulings of prophethood.
rows.anchor: بعنوان النبوة وأحكامها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects a fabricated Shiite reading of فانصب with kasra as commanding the appointment of Ali as imam, since an enemy could equally twist it into a command to hate him.
rows.anchor: ومن البدع ما روى عن بعض الرافضة أنه قرأ فانصب بكسر الصاد أي فانصب عليا للإمامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رغب فيه or إليه means desiring and earnestly seeking it, while رغب عنه means turning away; the verse means ask God alone, since only He can help.
rows.anchor: والمعنى فارغب بالسؤال ولا تسأل غيره فإنه القادر على إسعافك لا غيره

rows.speaker: بعض الأكابر
rows.claim: An esoteric reading makes expansion the lifting of ego and duality, the burden the shadow-self's extinction, and the Prophet's raised mention his annihilation in God and abiding through Him.
rows.anchor: وعن بعض الأكابر ألم نشرح لك صدرك برفع غطاء أنيتك وكشف حجاب أثنينيتك

rows.speaker: بعض الأكابر
rows.claim: The same reading counsels accepting decree, enduring trials, and thanking for gifts: hardship and ease accompany one another, and neither pleasure nor pain should veil the seeker.
rows.anchor: فارض بالقضاء واصبر على البلاء واشكر على النعماء فإن مع عسر الابتلاء بالبلايا

rows.speaker: بعض الأكابر
rows.claim: Give each present moment its due, prepare for the next, and continue until death, desiring God's majesty and beauty rather than being veiled by passing matters.
rows.anchor: فإذا فرغت من إعطاء حق وارد كل وقت حاضر فانصب نفسك في منصب إعطاء وارد

rows.speaker: طاوس
rows.claim: Tawus and Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz treated al-Duha and ألم نشرح as one surah and joined them in one prayer unit without the basmala.
rows.anchor: وعن طاووس وعمر بن عبد العزيز رحمهما الله إنهما كانا يقولان إن الضحى وألم نشرح سورة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects their view: the first surah depicts the Prophet's distress from unbelievers, while this one describes an opened chest and comfort, so their states differ.
rows.anchor: لأن تلك حال غتمامه عليه السلام بأذى الكفار فهي حال محنة وضيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fig is a fruit, food, and medicine; dream interpretations associate receiving it with wealth, eating it with children, and taking an olive leaf with holding the firm bond.
rows.anchor: وأما الزيتون فهو فاكهة وإدام ودواء ولو لم يكن له سوى اختصاصه

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Muadh took an olive twig as a tooth-stick and reported the Prophet's praise of olive wood as his own and earlier prophets' tooth-stick.
rows.anchor: ومر معاذ بن جبل رضي الله عنه بشجرة الزيتون فأخذ منها قضيبا وساتاك به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The olive tree is said to live three thousand years, withstand drought, and ripen more richly in dusty ground; its leaf ash helps the eyes.
rows.anchor: وشجرة الزيتون تعمر ثلاثة آلاف سنة ومن خواصها أنها تصبر عن الماء طويلا

rows.speaker: رسول الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report recommends olive oil to clear bile and phlegm, strengthen nerves, prevent fainting, improve character, and relieve worry.
rows.anchor: يكشف المرة ويذهب البلغم ويشد العصب ويمنع الغشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of Ibn Sirin tells a sick man to eat olives after a healing dream, alluding to the tree that is neither eastern nor western.
rows.anchor: وقال مريض لابن سيرين رأيت في المنام كأنه قيل لي كل اللاءين تشفى

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari identifies the fig with Mount Qasyun near Damascus and the olive with Mount Zayta east of Jerusalem, where the respective trees grow.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبري المراد بالتين الجبل الذي عليه دمشق يعني جبل الصالحية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mount Sinai is the place where Moses spoke with God; the word طور applies properly to a mountain with trees and fruit, while Sinai and Sinin name its region.
rows.anchor: هو الجبل الذي ناجى عليه موسى عليه السلام ربه

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi says a mountain is called طور only if it has trees and fruit; otherwise it is merely a mountain, and Sinīn or Sinai names its location.
rows.anchor: قال الماوردي : ليس كل جبل يقال له طورا لا أن يكون

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Kashf al-Asrar gives Sinīn as a rhyme-driven form of Sinai, like al-Yasin for Ilyas at the end of another surah; the name means wooded, beautiful, or blessed.
rows.anchor: وفي "كشف الأسرار" أصل سينين سيناء بفتح السين وكسرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secure town is Mecca: it protects those entering from killing and attack, and the Prophet's report says one dying in either sanctuary is raised safely.
rows.anchor: أي الآمن يقال أمن الرجل بضم الميم أمانة فهو أمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath honors blessed places where prophets lived: Abraham migrated and Jesus was born and raised near the fig and olive, Moses was called at Sinai, and Muhammad was born and commissioned in Mecca.
rows.anchor: ومعنى القسم بهذه الأشياء الإبانة عن شرف البقاع المباركة وما ظهر فيها من الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question expresses astonishment that anyone would accuse the Prophet of lying about recompense after the clear signs of resurrection; every denier of truth becomes a liar.
rows.anchor: أي فأي شيء يكذبك يا محمد دلالة أو نطقا بالجزاء بعد ظهور هذه الدلائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's creation of a sound human from a lowly fluid, growth to maturity, and decline to old age plainly proves His power to resurrect and recompense.
rows.anchor: فإن من خلق الإنسان السوي من الماء المهين وجعل ظاهره وباطنه على أحسن تقويم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the question addresses the human being: what could make you lie by denying the Judgment after this proof?
rows.anchor: أو فما يجعلك أيها الإنسان كاذبا بسبب الدين وإنكاره بعد هذا الدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The One who formed humanity so perfectly is the most precise in creation and governance; His power and knowledge entail resurrection and judgment.
rows.anchor: أي أليس الذي فعل ما ذكر بأحكم الحاكمين صنعا وتدبيرا حتى يتوهم عدم الإعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes أحكم الحاكمين as the chief judge who rules justly between the Prophet and those denying the truth, threatening their punishment.
rows.anchor: أو المعنى أليس الله بأقضى القاضين يحكم بينك وبين من يكذبك بالحق العدل

rows.speaker: رسول الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Outside prayer, the Prophet answered the verse by saying yes and bearing witness; he also instructed reciters to respond the same way.
rows.anchor: وكان عليه السلام إذا قرأها يقول بلى وأنا على ذلك من الشاهدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report promises health and certainty in this world to whoever recites the surah and reward proportional to its reciters.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ هذه السورة إعطاه الله خصلتين العافية واليقين ما دام في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God the Creator recalls the first blessing and proves that the One who gave humanity life and its perfections can teach reading; creation belongs solely to Him.
rows.anchor: وصف الرب به لتذكير أول النعماء الفائضة عليه منه تعالى والتنبيه على أن من قدر على خلق الإنسان

rows.speaker: فتح الرحمن
rows.claim: Fath al-Rahman says the Creator attribute answers Arabs who called idols lords, since idols cannot share in creating.
rows.anchor: وقال في فتح الرحمن لما ذكر الرب وكانت العرب في الجاهلية تسمى الأصنام أربابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity is singled out either for its wondrous creation or its nobility as the recipient of revelation; the first creation clause may be broad and the second an explanation.
rows.anchor: على الاول تخصيص لخلق الانسان بالذكر من بين سائر المخلوقات لاستقلاله ببدآئع الصنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: علق is the plural of علقة, a clinging, moist clot of congealed blood; the plural treats generic humanity collectively and suits the verse endings.
rows.anchor: جمع علقة كثمر وثمرة وهى الدم الجامد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clot highlights the striking gap between humanity's first state and final form, proving divine power; human creation is a primary blessing and evidence of God's existence, knowledge, and wisdom.
rows.anchor: لبيان كمال قدرته تعالى باظهار ما بين حالته الأولى والآخرة من التباين البين

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says God first made the polytheists acknowledge that they were created from a clot, which they could not deny or attribute to idols, then led them to admit the Creator alone deserves worship.
rows.anchor: حواشي ابن الشيخ إن الحكيم سبحانه لما أراد أن يبعثه رسولا إلى المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same method resembles Abu Hanifa's advice to Zufar: present opponents' views and weaknesses before identifying the sound position as Abu Hanifa's, so listeners will accept it.
rows.anchor: ومن هذه الطريقة ما يحكى أن زفر لما بعثه أبو حنيفة رحمه الله إلى البصرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iqra is a command, repeated to reinforce the obligation and introduce a new sentence about the most generous Lord; a permissible pause follows خلق because the Prophet had objected that he could not read.
rows.anchor: وكرر علامة الأمر بالقراءة تأكيدا للإيجاب وتمهيدا لما يعقبه من قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is more generous than every generous person, gives without motive or desire for praise, and is the source from whom all others receive generosity.
rows.anchor: وهو الأكرم أي الزائد في الكرم على كل كريم فإنه ينعم بلا غرض ولا يطلب مدحا

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh parses ربك as the subject, الأكرم as its adjective, and the relative clause as its predicate.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الشيخ : ربك مبتدأ والأكرم صفته والذي مع صلته خبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God taught by means of the pen while teaching the Prophet without writing; others explain the phrase as teaching handwriting and script through the cutting nib.
rows.anchor: أي علم ما علم بواسطة القلم لا غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teaching writing is a favor to humanity; knowledge is a catch and writing its tether, and the poem urges writers to leave only what they would wish to see at Judgment.
rows.anchor: وفيه امتنان على الإنسان بتعليم علم الخط والكتابة بالقلم ولذلك قيل العلم صيد

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Kaab al-Ahbar reports that Adam wrote Arabic, Syriac, and all books in clay three hundred years before death, later recovered by Idris; Idris invented sand writing, Tahmurth Persian writing, and Joseph papyrus.
rows.anchor: قال كعب الأحبار أول من وضع الكتاب العربي والسرياني والكتب كلها آدم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: السيوطي
rows.claim: Al-Suyuti says God commanded the first created pen to record everything destined until Judgment Day, beginning with God's promise to forgive whoever repents.
rows.anchor: قال السيوطي رحمه الله أول ما خلق الله القلم قال له اكتب ما هو كائن

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One explanation contrasts humanity's lowly beginning as a clot with its highest rank as learned; another links the clot to primordial divine love and the hidden treasure's wish to be known.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم وجه المناسبة بين الخلق من العق وتعليم القلم أن أدنى مراتب الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause specifies what God taught, by pen and directly: every kind of universal, particular, manifest, and hidden knowledge beyond prior imagination.
rows.anchor: بدل اشتمال من علم بالقلم وتعيين للمفعول أي علمه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet did not write lest people accuse him of copying earlier scriptures; served by the highest pen and Preserved Tablet, he needed no physical writing instrument.
rows.anchor: فإذا كان القلم والخط من المن الإلهية فما باله عليه السلام لم يكتب قلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, Muhammad's community is spiritual among nations, with its scripture in its hearts; its readiness lets it preserve the law even without written marks.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة بديعة إلى أن أمته بين الأمم هم الروحانيون وصفهم سبحانه في الإنجيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rebukes anyone who rejects God's favor through transgression, even if no person was previously named, for emphatic warning; al-Sajawandi also reads it as حقا and pauses before it.
rows.anchor: ردع لمن كفر بنعمة الله عليه بطغيانه وإن لم يسبق ذكره للمبالغة

rows.speaker: السجاوتدي
rows.claim: Al-Sajawandi recommends pausing after ما لم يعلم because he understands كلا to mean حقا.
rows.anchor: وقال السجاوتدي يوقف على ما لم يعلم لأنه بمعنى حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human being crosses limits and grows arrogant toward his Lord; the verse identifies what is being rebuked and restrained.
rows.anchor: أي يتجاوز الحد ويستكبر على ربه بيان للمردوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage from this verse to the chapter's end is said to have descended later about Abu Jahl; the wording can also encompass his peers and Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: قيل إن هذا إلى آخر السورة نزل في أبي جهل بعد زمان وهو الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person transgresses because he believes or sees himself as self-sufficient; the wording may describe Abu Jahl and his companions or Pharaoh's claim to divinity.
rows.anchor: مفعول له أي يطغى لأن رأى وعلم نفسه مستغنيا أو أبصر مثل أبي جهل
